Obrador scores 5.5/10 because the 2022 record combines some competent, broadly beneficial stewardship with serious weaknesses in investment conditions, market neutrality, productivity foundations, and demonstrated policy correction. Positive evidence includes a broadly neutral fiscal stance judged appropriate by the IMF, income and employment improvements, and falling labor poverty (E069, E074). The administration also maintained a qualified professional finance appointment, although independence was not established (E068). Against this, regulatory uncertainty constrained private investment, executive-led energy and state-firm policies generated a formal USMCA challenge, and infrastructure and electricity constraints limited the conversion of nearshoring opportunity into durable growth (E006, E071, E072). Inflation was substantially shock-driven and Banxico remained autonomous, so neither should be assigned wholesale to AMLO (E008, E075). Distributional gains were real but incomplete, and evidence-based correction is weakly documented (E073). A lower 5.0 is rejected because attributable stabilization and household improvements outweigh a failure-level judgment; a higher 6.0 is rejected because capture concerns, weak correction evidence,
